title: Philippine Bank Regulatory Reporting
thesis: Snowflake turns daily regulatory-reporting data checks for a fictional Philippine bank into exception-precision KPIs, 7-day material-error risk scores, late-feed anomalies, sign-off and lineage coverage and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Exception precision, exceptions raised, material errors and escalated items for 40 reporting units across Makati City, Cebu City, Davao City, Iloilo City and Cagayan de Oro.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to reporting-unit-day rows.
The validation-rule chart shows which internal checks find material errors and which mostly raise false positives.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of reporting data-quality KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which units should the reporting team check first before the next submission?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each reporting unit's probability of a material reporting error in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags late source-feed outliers per unit, and the forecast projects bank-wide exception volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are sign-offs and source-feed lineage keeping up?

talking_points: Controller sign-off compliance, feed mapping coverage and feeds pending mapping frame the control gaps.
Sign-off compliance against material errors by unit shows where weak sign-off discipline and errors move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, reporting-unit, validation-rule and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a source extract fails its checks right now?

talking_points: Live source-feed loads land in RAW.LIVE_EVENTS, from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs loads with failed validation checks, adds an SOP hint and the unit's current risk band, then emails the reporting team.
tabs.call_out: From failed extract to ticket in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 14 synthetic exception-handling SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited. The SOPs are internal procedures of the fictional bank, not BSP text.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
